requirements.quote: When a TCP/IP socket connection is established between the client and the broker, a protocol level session is required.
requirements.condition: A TCP/IP socket connection has been established between a client and broker.
requirements.required_behavior: Establish a protocol-level session over the connection.
requirements.why_checkable: A connection/session test can verify that the implementation enters protocol-session processing after socket establishment.

requirements.quote:
byte 1	Message Type (1)	DUP flag	QoS level	RETAIN

0	0	0	1	x	x	x	x
requirements.condition: A CONNECT fixed header is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or recognize the four-bit Message Type value as 1 (binary 0001).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat another Message Type value as CONNECT.
requirements.why_checkable: The first fixed-header byte can be inspected to verify the CONNECT type bits.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS, and RETAIN flags are not used in the CONNECT message.
requirements.condition: A CONNECT message is processed or produced.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign CONNECT semantics to the DUP, QoS, or RETAIN flags.
requirements.why_checkable: Static or runtime inspection can determine whether these flag fields affect CONNECT processing.

requirements.quote: Remaining Length is the length of the variable header (12 bytes) and the length of the Payload.
requirements.condition: A CONNECT Remaining Length field is calculated or validated.
requirements.required_behavior: Set or validate Remaining Length as 12 bytes plus the encoded Payload length.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded Remaining Length can be compared with the 12-byte variable header and actual payload size.

requirements.quote: This can be a multibyte field.
requirements.condition: The CONNECT Remaining Length value requires more than one encoded byte.
requirements.required_behavior: Support a multibyte Remaining Length field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assume that CONNECT Remaining Length is always a single byte.
requirements.why_checkable: A CONNECT packet with a sufficiently large payload can test multibyte Remaining Length handling.

requirements.quote: The first UTF-encoded string. The Client Identifier (Client ID) is between 1 and 23 characters long, and uniquely identifies the client to the broker.
requirements.condition: A CONNECT payload is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Place or interpret the Client Identifier as the first UTF-encoded string and require its length to be between 1 and 23 characters inclusive.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept or emit a Client Identifier outside the 1-to-23-character range as valid.
requirements.why_checkable: Payload parsing can verify the first field's UTF encoding and character-count bounds.

requirements.quote: It must be unique across all clients connecting to a single broker, and is the key in handling Message IDs messages with QoS levels 1 and 2.
requirements.condition: Multiple clients connect to the same broker.
requirements.required_behavior: Ensure each connected client has a unique Client Identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Maintain simultaneous clients with the same Client Identifier as distinct valid identities.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime test can connect multiple clients using the same identifier and inspect the broker's identity/session handling.

requirements.quote: If the Client ID contains more than 23 characters, the broker responds to the CONNECT message with a CONNACK return code 2: Identifier Rejected.
requirements.condition: A broker receives a CONNECT whose Client ID contains more than 23 characters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept the overlength identifier or respond with a different CONNACK return code.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with CONNACK return code 2, Identifier Rejected.
requirements.why_checkable: A CONNECT containing a 24-or-more-character Client ID has a deterministic response code.

requirements.quote: The Will Message is published to the Will Topic.
requirements.condition: The broker executes a client's Will Message.
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message to the Will Topic.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Publish the Will Message to a different topic.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can trigger Will execution and observe the topic on which the broker publishes it.

requirements.quote: The QoS level is defined by the Will QoS field, and the RETAIN status is defined by the Will RETAIN flag in the variable header.
requirements.condition: A Will Message is configured or published.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Will QoS field as the Will publication's QoS level and the variable-header Will RETAIN flag as its RETAIN status.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Derive the Will publication's QoS or RETAIN status from different fields.
requirements.why_checkable: The Will publication's observed QoS and retain state can be compared with the originating CONNECT fields.

requirements.quote: The Will Message defines the content of the message that is published to the Will Topic if the client is unexpectedly disconnected.
requirements.condition: A client with a configured Will Message is unexpectedly disconnected.
requirements.required_behavior: Publish the Will Message content to the Will Topic.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Substitute different content when executing the Will after an unexpected disconnect.
requirements.why_checkable: A runtime disconnect test can compare the configured Will content with the resulting publication.

requirements.quote: Although the Will Message is UTF-encoded in the CONNECT message, when it is published to the Will Topic only the bytes of the message are sent, not the first two length bytes.
requirements.condition: A broker publishes a Will Message received as a UTF-encoded CONNECT field.
requirements.required_behavior: Publish only the message bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include the UTF field's first two length bytes in the published payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The resulting publication payload can be byte-compared with the CONNECT field after removing its two-byte length prefix.

requirements.quote: The message sent when the broker executes the Will Message is raw ASCII, not UTF-encoded.
requirements.condition: The broker executes a Will Message.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the Will Message as raw ASCII.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the executed Will Message as a UTF-encoded field.
requirements.why_checkable: Wire-level inspection can determine whether the sent message is raw data or includes UTF field encoding.

requirements.quote: The broker sends a CONNACK message in response to a CONNECT message from a client.
requirements.condition: A broker receives a CONNECT message from a client.
requirements.required_behavior: Send a CONNACK response.
requirements.why_checkable: A protocol test can send CONNECT and observe whether the next broker response is CONNACK.

requirements.quote: If the client does not receive a CONNACK message from the broker within a "reasonable" amount of time, the client closes the TCP/IP socket connection, and restarts the session by opening a socket to the broker and issuing a CONNECT message.
requirements.condition: The client's implementation-defined reasonable response interval expires without receiving CONNACK.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the existing TCP/IP socket, open a new socket to the broker, and issue a new CONNECT to restart the session.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Continue indefinitely on the original socket without restarting the session.
requirements.why_checkable: With the configured timeout known, a test can withhold CONNACK and observe socket closure and reconnection behavior.

requirements.quote:
byte 1	Message type (2)	DUP flag	QoS flags	RETAIN

0	0	1	0	x	x	x	x
requirements.condition: A CONNACK fixed header is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or recognize the four-bit Message Type value as 2 (binary 0010).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat another Message Type value as CONNACK.
requirements.why_checkable: The first fixed-header byte can be inspected to verify the CONNACK type bits.

requirements.quote:
byte 2	Remaining Length (2)

0	0	0	0	0	0	1	0
requirements.condition: A CONNACK message is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or require Remaining Length to equal 2.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat another Remaining Length as the defined CONNACK structure.
requirements.why_checkable: The second fixed-header byte has a directly inspectable fixed value of 2.

requirements.quote: The DUP, QoS and RETAIN flags are not used in the CONNACK message.
requirements.condition: A CONNACK message is processed or produced.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign CONNACK semantics to the DUP, QoS, or RETAIN flags.
requirements.why_checkable: Static or runtime inspection can determine whether these flag fields affect CONNACK processing.

requirements.quote: byte 1	Reserved values. Not used.	x	x	x	x	x	x	x	x
requirements.condition: The first byte of a CONNACK variable header is processed or produced.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the reserved first variable-header byte to convey or control protocol behavior.
requirements.why_checkable: Tests or code inspection can determine whether this byte influences CONNACK semantics.

requirements.quote: The values for the one byte unsigned Connect return code field are shown in the table below.
requirements.condition: A CONNACK Connect Return Code is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the Connect Return Code as a one-byte unsigned field.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Encode the Connect Return Code with a different width or signed representation.
requirements.why_checkable: Wire inspection can verify that exactly one unsigned byte is used for the field.

requirements.quote: 0	0x00	Connection Accepted
requirements.condition: A CONNACK return code of 0x00 is processed or emitted.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret or emit 0x00 as Connection Accepted.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign a refusal meaning to return code 0x00.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's mapping for the byte value 0x00 can be tested directly.

requirements.quote: 1	0x01	Connection Refused: unacceptable protocol version
requirements.condition: A CONNACK return code of 0x01 is processed or emitted.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret or emit 0x01 as connection refused because of an unacceptable protocol version.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign a different meaning to return code 0x01.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's mapping for the byte value 0x01 can be tested directly.

requirements.quote: 2	0x02	Connection Refused: identifier rejected
requirements.condition: A CONNACK return code of 0x02 is processed or emitted.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret or emit 0x02 as connection refused because the identifier was rejected.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign a different meaning to return code 0x02.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's mapping for the byte value 0x02 can be tested directly.

requirements.quote: 3	0x03	Connection Refused: broker unavailable
requirements.condition: A CONNACK return code of 0x03 is processed or emitted.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret or emit 0x03 as connection refused because the broker is unavailable.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assign a different meaning to return code 0x03.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's mapping for the byte value 0x03 can be tested directly.

requirements.quote: 4-255	Reserved for future use
requirements.condition: A Connect Return Code is selected for emission under this protocol version.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use values 4 through 255 as currently defined Connect Return Codes.
requirements.why_checkable: Generated CONNACK messages can be checked for use of reserved return-code values.

requirements.quote: Return code 2 (identifier rejected) is sent if the unique client identifier is not between 1 and 23 characters in length.
requirements.condition: The unique Client Identifier is shorter than 1 character or longer than 23 characters.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Accept the identifier or send a different return code.
requirements.error_behavior: Send Connect Return Code 2, identifier rejected.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary tests using zero-, one-, 23-, and 24-character identifiers can verify the response code.

requirements.quote: There is no payload.
requirements.condition: A CONNACK message is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or require an empty payload.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include or accept payload data as part of the defined CONNACK message.
requirements.why_checkable: The bytes following the two-byte variable header can be inspected for absence of payload.

requirements.quote: Each PUBLISH message is associated with a topic name (also known as the Subject or Channel).
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message is encoded, decoded, or distributed.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the message with a topic name.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat a PUBLISH message as lacking a topic association.
requirements.why_checkable: PUBLISH parsing and internal message state can be inspected for a topic-name association.

requirements.quote: A message that is published to a specific topic name is delivered to connected subscribers for that topic.
requirements.condition: A message is published to a topic having connected subscribers.
requirements.required_behavior: Deliver the message to the connected subscribers for that topic.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Route the message solely to subscribers of unrelated topics.
requirements.why_checkable: A broker test can establish subscriptions, publish on the topic, and observe recipient delivery.

requirements.quote: To maintain symmetry, if a client subscribes to one or more topics, any message published to those topics are sent by the broker to the client as a PUBLISH message.
requirements.condition: A client is subscribed to one or more topics and a message is published to one of those topics.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the message from the broker to that client as a PUBLISH message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a different MQTT command-message type to deliver the subscribed publication.
requirements.why_checkable: A subscription-and-publish test can inspect the message type delivered by the broker.

requirements.quote:
byte 1	Message type (3)	DUP flag	QoS level	RETAIN

0	0	1	1	0	0	1	0
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH fixed header is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode or recognize the four-bit Message Type value as 3 (binary 0011).
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat another Message Type value as PUBLISH.
requirements.why_checkable: The first fixed-header byte can be masked and inspected for the PUBLISH type bits.

requirements.quote: For messages with QoS level 1 or level 2 that are being re-sent because a failure has been detected, the DUP bit is set to 1.
requirements.condition: A QoS level 1 or 2 PUBLISH message is retransmitted because a failure was detected.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the DUP bit to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Retransmit the message under this condition with DUP clear.
requirements.why_checkable: A failure-and-retransmission test can inspect the DUP bit on the retransmitted packet.

requirements.quote: This indicates to the broker that the message might duplicate a message that has already been received.
requirements.condition: A broker receives a PUBLISH message with DUP set to 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the flag as indicating that the message might duplicate an already received message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat DUP=1 as proof that the message is necessarily new.
requirements.why_checkable: Broker duplicate-handling logic can be inspected or exercised with repeated packet transmissions.

requirements.quote: The DUP bit is not used for messages with QoS level 0.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message has QoS level 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the DUP bit to control or infer QoS 0 message semantics.
requirements.why_checkable: Runtime tests can vary the DUP bit on QoS 0 input and determine whether it affects processing.

requirements.quote: A Message ID must not be used in the variable header for messages with QoS level 0.
requirements.condition: A PUBLISH message has QoS level 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include or use a Message ID in the variable header.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed or emitted QoS 0 variable header can be inspected for absence of a Message ID.
